# Pedestals

A **trophy pedestal** records an achievement: one of the mod's own feats, an advancement, or anything else another mod
registers a kind of trophy for ([Trophy kinds](for-mods.md#trophy-kinds-for-mods)). Placed, it shows the achievement's icon turning above it,
glowing like a hologram, with its rank's light round it ([Ranks](ranks.md)); floating over it are its rank, what it
records in its color, who earned it (a player, their team, or "the whole server") and when, in the reader's own date format. The text sits on a panel in its rank's frame, and shows while a player looks at the pedestal within their reach. Sneaking and using a pedestal with an empty hand opens its adjustment screen, a trophy's in tabs (Display: size, height, yaw, pitch and roll, and a legendary trophy's crown position; Effects: the showcase light, when its flourishes show, and a legendary trophy's crown; Text: when it shows, its height, its size; Behavior: spinning, sounds and redstone; Pose, for a mob or statue: its pose and animation): its text shows when looked at, always (within 32 blocks) or never, its item or mob can be shown from half to twenty times its usual size (its light, outlines, flare, beam, halos, crown and particles grow with it), moved from half a block down to ten blocks up and turned to face any way; it can stand still instead of spinning; a mob trophy's mob can hold one pose instead of moving (Mob Pose: Frozen, which stops a blaze's rods and an allay's wings); an achievement trophy earned by a player can show that player's statue, in their own skin, in place of its icon (Display: Statue), standing, crouching, swimming, gliding or sleeping (the button beside it; a player trophy's is beside Mob Pose); a mob or statue can play one animation on loop, picked from a list found from the mob itself (Animation: walking, running and attacking where its model moves for them, its own animations like a warden's roar or a camel sitting down, its own states like a fox sitting or sleeping, and its own poses like a parrot's; choosing one sets a frozen mob moving); its text can be shown from half to three times its usual size, frame and all (Text Size); its flourishes (its rank's beam, halos, crown shards, flares and particles, or its lens's effects) show always (the default), only while looked at, or never (Effects: Flourishes), its showcase light, outlines and a lens's colour showing either way; its showcase light (the lit lens, the cone of light rising out of the well and its frame) can be turned off too, on a trophy or a display pedestal (Showcase Light); its sounds can be turned off; its text can be moved up or down; and it can answer redstone, showing its display only while powered or hiding it then. Each section's name has a ? beside it that explains the option while hovered, and so does each Behavior button. A display pedestal's screen has the same Effects tab. Each slider has a button putting it back, and Reset puts everything back. Mods can set a pedestal's settings and lock them with `net.ixdarklord.trophypedestals.api.PedestalSettings` (`set`, `lock`, `force`, `unlock`; `PedestalBlocks.pedestalAt` finds the pedestal at a position): a locked pedestal's screen opens for no one, its owner and operators included, and a player who tries is told the mod's message in their action bar ("This pedestal's settings are locked" unless it gives its own), or is refused silently. Who may adjust it is the server's `pedestals.access` setting: `OWNER` (the default: the player who placed it, and operators; anyone, for a pedestal placed before pedestals had owners) or `ANYONE`. The item's tooltip says the same, and breaking the pedestal keeps its record.

Pedestals come in vanilla's stones and woods (`trophypedestals:<material>_pedestal`): stone, cobblestone, mossy cobblestone,
cobbled deepslate, deepslate, blackstone, stone bricks, bricks, mud bricks, resin bricks, nether bricks, red nether
bricks, granite, diorite, andesite, calcite, tuff, basalt, end stone, purpur, prismarine, dark prismarine, sandstone, red
sandstone and quartz, and oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, pale oak, bamboo, crimson and
warped. An empty one is crafted from six of its material, a lens on top and a gold ingot at the base (recipe type
`trophypedestals:pedestal`, which keeps the lens; `data/trophypedestals/recipe/<material>_pedestal.json`,
which a data pack can replace); a stone one is mined with a pickaxe, a wooden one with an axe.

Any other block, a mod's stones and woods included, makes a **custom pedestal** (`trophypedestals:custom_pedestal`): one block
whose material is data, the `trophypedestals:pedestal_material` component naming the block it's made of. It's drawn with that
block's own textures (its top, bottom and sides, tinted as the block is), with the same gold carving and well as every
pedestal, and named after it ("Mossy Stone Bricks Pedestal"; give the item a `minecraft:item_name` for another name). A
data pack hands them out with a recipe, a loot table or `/give`, and breaking one keeps its material. The mod adds none of
its own; the example data pack (`testpack/`) has six, crafted like the others: amethyst block, obsidian, copper block,
mossy stone bricks, smooth stone and polished blackstone bricks (`data/trophypedestals_example/recipe/<block>_pedestal.json`).
A recipe of your own looks like this:

```json
{
  "type": "trophypedestals:pedestal",
  "key": {"L": "#trophypedestals:lenses", "G": "minecraft:gold_ingot", "S": "minecraft:amethyst_block"},
  "pattern": ["SLS", " S ", "SGS"],
  "result": {"id": "trophypedestals:custom_pedestal", "components": {"trophypedestals:pedestal_material": "minecraft:amethyst_block"}}
}
```

One with no material, or a block no longer in the game, is drawn as stone. Either tool mines it. It can be a trophy too
(`set_trophy` on one in a loot table, below), and works as any pedestal does. A crafted pedestal with a lens fitted displays any item put on it (with no lens it refuses, and says so; use it with the item in hand; use it with an empty hand to take it back), as a showcase: the item turns slowly in a soft cone of warm light rising out of the well, over a gently glowing frame; a named item shows its name over it while you look at it. The rising outlines, flare, beam and particles are a trophy's only. A trophy's well shows a dark glass lens in a gold bezel, which fades up to the rank's color once it holds something (and back down as it turns off); a display pedestal shows the fitted lens's glass in that bezel, or with no lens, an empty socket printed in its well, whose middle glows while its When Powered option has it on (always on Ignore, with redstone power on Show, without it on Hide); a pedestal gives a low light even when empty while that option has it on (level 6 with its socket open, 3 with a lens fitted), and one its When Powered option has off dims its lens; a fitted lens's glass breathes with light while the pedestal is on and showing something. Every pedestal's column is fluted.

A **lens** fitted to a display pedestal sets the look of its showcase. Every pedestal is crafted with one (any lens, in
the top middle of its recipe) and comes with it: placed, the lens is fitted, and broken, the pedestal keeps it in its
item. A display pedestal placed before lenses came has a Clear Lens. Use a lens on the top face of a display pedestal to swap it in
(the old one comes back); with an empty hand on its top, once no item is shown, take it out. Trophies and leaderboards keep their own looks. A mannequin shows its lens too, with Curator's going by the rarest piece it wears or holds, and a pedestal with no lens has the warm
light above.

| Lens | Recipe |
|---|---|
| Clear | 4 gold nuggets around a glass pane |
| Blood Moon | Clear Lens with rotten flesh above and below, redstone on its sides |
| Prism | Clear Lens with amethyst shards above and below, prismarine crystals on its sides |
| Coral Reef | Clear Lens with kelp at the top corners, a prismarine shard below |
| Curator's | Clear Lens with an emerald above, gold ingots on its sides |
| Inferno | Clear Lens with blaze powder above, a row of 3 coal below |
| Blizzard | Clear Lens with snowballs at the top corners, packed ice below |
| Void Rift | Clear Lens with an ender pearl above, popped chorus fruit on its sides and below |
| Cipher | Clear Lens with redstone at the top corners, a glow ink sac below |

The effects follow the pedestal's Flourishes setting: always (the default, particles within 32 blocks), only while looked
at, or never; none of the particles show in a glass case, where the item keeps still too.
Each player can keep just the lenses' colours with `lens_effects` in their client config; the moving parts also follow
`flourishes` and the pedestal's own flourishes setting.

A pedestal its When Powered option turns off keeps what it shows: a flat item lies down on the lens, a block sits upright on it, and a mob or statue settles on to the pedestal, each facing the way the pedestal was placed (as a furnace does), a little smaller and quite still, with no animation, light or effects, and rises again when it turns back on.

The **Curator's Stamp** (a stick, a gold ingot and an ink sac in a column) copies a pedestal to others. Sneak-use a pedestal to copy its settings and lens, use it on another to paste them, use the air to choose whether it pastes both, only the settings or only the lens before you copy, and sneak-use the air to clear it. The choice stays locked while the stamp holds a copy. Pasting follows the adjust screen's ownership, locks and server config, and never copies who may adjust a pedestal. A lens is only fitted to display pedestals; in survival it takes a matching one (same dye included) from your inventory and hands back the one it replaces, and without one the settings still paste.

## Trophy cabinets and shelves

A **trophy cabinet** (two blocks wide, half a block deep, holding four trophies; cabinets stacked on one another join)
and a **trophy shelf** (on the side of a solid block, holding two; shelves side by side join) come in every wood, plain,
with no trim. Use a block on one to trim it with that block: its rails, posts, corner caps and brackets are drawn in
that block's textures. A block with a block entity (a chest, a furnace, a pedestal, a mod's machine) is never a trim,
nor is one in the `trophypedestals:no_trim` block tag, which data packs can fill. A gold ingot (or a gold block) gives
the gold trim, and an axe takes the trim off again. The trim is the `trophypedestals:trim_material` component
(`minecraft:gold_block` for gold), kept when it's broken; a trimmed one's item shows its trim. Use a trophy on a spot to put it there, and an empty hand to take it back. Any item
that isn't a block goes on a spot too, standing there by itself (a block in hand is for the trim). Each spot can be
aimed at by itself, through the open front only: aiming through the rim, the sides, the back or the frame isn't aiming
at a trophy, so it neither takes it nor shows its text. Sneaking with an empty hand on a trophy opens its settings; on
anything else of the cabinet or shelf, the owner gets its **Cabinet Settings**: who else may use it (Private, the
default, Team, or Everyone; operators always can) and when the name of the set its trophies make shows over it (Shown,
the default, On Look, or Hidden). Whoever places one owns it (one placed before had no owner and stays open to anyone),
and only those its owner lets may put trophies on it, take them off, trim it or adjust them. Four different mobs of
one mod (not Minecraft's own) make that mod's set, "Aether II Set", with no data pack needed.
